chapters.name: Signs, Signals, and Pavement Markings
chapters.summary: What sign shapes and colors mean, how to respond to steady and flashing traffic lights, and what lane lines and other pavement markings tell you.
keyPoints: An eight-sided red sign means stop. A downward-pointing triangle means yield.
Yellow diamond signs warn of hazards ahead. Orange signs mark work zones.
A flashing red light means stop completely, then go when it is safe. A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

chapters.name: Right of Way and Turns
chapters.summary: Who goes first at intersections, four-way stops, and roundabouts, how to make turns correctly, and when you must yield to pedestrians and emergency vehicles.
keyPoints: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to stop goes first. If two arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.

chapters.name: Speed, Lanes, Passing, and Parking
chapters.summary: Texas speed limits, choosing a safe speed, lane use and passing, following distance, and where you may not park.
keyPoints: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit is 30 mph in an urban district and 15 mph in an alley.
Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes.
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

chapters.name: Safe Driving and Sharing the Road
chapters.summary: Driving at night and in bad weather, handling skids and emergencies, and sharing the road with school buses, trucks, motorcycles, bicycles, trains, and work zones.
keyPoints: Stop for a school bus with flashing red lights unless it is on the other side of a divided highway.
Use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
Large trucks have big blind spots. If you cannot see the truck driver in the truck's mirror, the driver cannot see you.

chapters.name: Licensing, Alcohol, and Driver Responsibility
chapters.summary: Graduated driver license rules for teens, insurance and crash duties, alcohol and drug laws, implied consent, phone use, and seat belts.
keyPoints: An adult is legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher. Drivers under 21 may not drive with any detectable amount of alcohol.
By driving in Texas, you agree to give a breath or blood specimen if arrested for driving while intoxicated (implied consent).
Texting while driving is illegal for all drivers in Texas, and drivers under 18 may not use any wireless communication device.
